Issue: Toxic purchased backlink profile
Evidence: Semrush: 103 ref domains / 222 backlinks. 99% of ref domains at Authority Score 0-10. 78% of ref domains in Singapore, 13% .in TLD. 103 domains resolve to only 52 IPs / 48 subnets. Anchor report contains "fiverr helped {panamarealestateguide.com} rank #1 for over 50 targeted keywords", "with fiverr's help, panamarealestateguide.com saw a sales increase of 200%", "trusted backlink strategy...feedback included". Network Graph flagged Dangerous.
Expected_Impact: Removes the largest single obstacle to ranking. A profile this synthetic caps trust no matter how good the content is.
Implementation_Guidance: 1) Stop any active link purchase immediately. 2) Export the full backlink list from Semrush and Search Console. 3) Classify: keep genuine editorial links only. 4) Submit a domain-level disavow file for the PBN/Fiverr clusters via Google Disavow Tool. 5) Re-audit monthly. Do NOT attempt removal outreach to these sellers.
Risk: Medium — over-disavowing genuine links loses equity. Have a second reviewer confirm the keep/disavow list before upload.
Validation_Method: Re-run Semrush Backlink Audit after 60 days; ref-domain AS distribution should shift; monitor Search Console Manual Actions

Issue: 73% of indexed URLs are machine-translated duplicates — delete them
Evidence: Sitemap: 556 URLs, of which 405 are /es/, /de/, /pt/. These earned 30 clicks combined in 119 days (~0.25/day) across 24 URLs. Semrush shows /de/articles/panama-vs-costa-rica-retirement.html ranking for the English query "retire in panama vs costa rica" at position 88, and /es/ and / versions both ranking for "internet panama" (pos 86 and 69) — the translations compete with their own originals. Semrush Top Pages confirms 0 referring domains on every deep URL (93 of 103 ref domains point at the root), so no page-level link equity exists to preserve.
Expected_Impact: Removes self-cannibalisation and lifts site-wide quality signals by deleting 405 thin pages. Note: crawl budget is NOT a meaningful factor at 556 URLs — the benefit is quality and cannibalisation, not crawl efficiency.
Implementation_Guidance: Return 410 Gone for all /es/, /de/, /pt/ URLs (not 404 — 410 is unambiguous and de-indexed faster; 404 is retried for months on the assumption of error). Remove them from sitemap.xml. Remove hreflang annotations in the SAME deploy (see T-16). Retain the source files in git so the content is recoverable even though the URLs are not. Do not redirect to English equivalents — the content differs and mass redirects to loosely-related pages are treated as soft 404s.
Risk: Low. Costs 30 clicks/119d. Irreversible at the URL level, so ship as its own change roughly 2 weeks clear of the v2 cutover and the disavow, to keep the before/after readable.
Validation_Method: Search Console Pages report: indexed count should fall toward ~139; confirm 410 status on a sample via curl -I; watch Pages > 'Not found (404)' vs 'Page removed because of legal complaint' classifications

Issue: v2 rebuild changes every URL with no redirect map
Evidence: v1 live URLs are /articles/*.html, /news/*.html, /projects/*.html. v2 (Next.js, branch v2-redesign) routes are /[category]/[slug], /areas/[slug], /projects/[slug] — extensionless and re-parented. v2 has no middleware.ts and no redirect configuration.
Expected_Impact: Prevents total loss of the site's existing rankings and the 32 clicks/28d baseline at launch.
Implementation_Guidance: Before launch, produce a 1:1 old->new map for all 139 English URLs. Implement as permanent redirects in next.config.ts `redirects()` (or Netlify _redirects with 301). Every consolidated URL from the pruning sheet redirects to its stated destination. Never chain more than one hop. Retain the .html source URLs as redirect origins indefinitely.
Risk: High if skipped — this is the single largest risk in the project.
Validation_Method: Crawl the old URL list post-launch and assert every URL returns a single 301 to a 200. Monitor Search Console Pages > 'Page with redirect' and 404 counts daily for 30 days.

Issue: v2 has no XML sitemap and no robots.txt
Evidence: Checked v2/app: app/sitemap.ts MISSING, app/robots.ts MISSING, app/sitemap.xml/route.ts MISSING.
Expected_Impact: Without these, discovery of the rebuilt site depends entirely on internal linking.
Implementation_Guidance: Add app/sitemap.ts returning a MetadataRoute.Sitemap generated from Supabase (articles, areas, projects) with real lastModified values. Add app/robots.ts pointing to it. Note: this Next.js version has breaking changes — read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before implementing per the repo's AGENTS.md.
Risk: Low
Validation_Method: Fetch /sitemap.xml and /robots.txt on the deployed build; submit sitemap in Search Console and confirm 'Success' with expected URL count

Issue: v2 has almost no structured data
Evidence: grep for application/ld+json across v2/app, v2/components, v2/lib returns exactly one match (projects/[slug]/page.tsx:170). v1 by comparison emits Article, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage and VideoObject on article pages.
Expected_Impact: Losing schema at migration would be a regression against the current site.
Implementation_Guidance: Port and correct: Organization + WebSite on the root layout; BreadcrumbList on every nested page; Article with real author/datePublished/dateModified on guides; Person on author pages; Place on area hubs. For project pages use Residence or Product/Offer only where price and availability are genuinely visible on the page.
Risk: Low, but only mark up what is visibly on the page — invented schema risks a structured-data manual action.
Validation_Method: Google Rich Results Test + Search Console Enhancements reports; validate every template once

Issue: FAQPage markup is valid schema but not rich-result eligible
Evidence: v1 article pages emit FAQPage with 5 questions. Since Google's August 2023 change, FAQ rich results are shown only for authoritative government and health sites.
Expected_Impact: Sets correct expectations — keeping it costs nothing but it will not produce SERP real estate.
Implementation_Guidance: Keep FAQPage for semantic/LLM value if desired, but do not count it toward rich-result goals or CTR forecasts. Prioritise BreadcrumbList and Article, which remain eligible.
Risk: None
Validation_Method: Rich Results Test will validate the markup but report no eligible rich result — that is expected, not a bug

Issue: Mismatched VideoObject schema on article pages
Evidence: /articles/boquete-panama-real-estate.html (English, en-US) embeds VideoObject for a Spanish-language Pino Alto promo (inLanguage es-PA, duration PT3S).
Expected_Impact: Removes a mismatched-content signal and a 3-second video being presented as page media.
Implementation_Guidance: Only emit VideoObject where the video is genuinely about the page topic and is the page's primary or supporting media. Remove the 3-second promos from schema entirely; a PT3S video adds no value and may be treated as thin video content.
Risk: Low
Validation_Method: Rich Results Test on affected templates; Search Console Video indexing report

Issue: Duplicate directory and index.html URLs
Evidence: Sitemap and GSC contain both /articles/ and /articles/index.html, and both /news/ and /news/index.html, with impressions split across both.
Expected_Impact: Consolidates split signals on hub pages.
Implementation_Guidance: 301 /articles/index.html -> /articles/ and /news/index.html -> /news/. Remove the index.html forms from the sitemap. Ensure the canonical on each hub points to the trailing-slash form.
Risk: Low
Validation_Method: curl -I each index.html URL and assert 301; confirm only one form remains in the sitemap

Issue: 16 standalone /videos/ URLs are thin YouTube wrappers
Evidence: Sitemap contains 16 /videos/* URLs (plus 51 translated copies). GSC shows the best of them at 3 impressions / 1 click over 119 days. Separate sitemap-videos.xml declares 12 URLs.
Expected_Impact: Removes index bloat with no traffic cost.
Implementation_Guidance: noindex the standalone video URLs and embed the videos on the relevant area and project pages instead, where they add page value. Retire sitemap-videos.xml or reduce it to videos that live on substantive pages.
Risk: Low
Validation_Method: Search Console indexed-page count; confirm no click loss on the affected URLs

Issue: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-01: /proyectos/ canonical URLs were 404ing
Evidence: Supersedes the earlier 'do not redirect' correction. Two things were wrong. (1) The 4 pages are not project pages: each is a templated Spanish ad-campaign landing (Calendly embed, WhatsApp CTA, 9 utm_ params) hreflang'd to its /co/ and /es/ siblings. Three of the four names (sanctuary-residences, euphoria-art-district, casa-korsi-casco-antiguo) do not exist in the 31-project Airtable inventory, and all four reuse a real project's photography. (2) v2/public/_redirects already mapped the .html form, so 'NOT redirected' was false post-cutover, but the extensionless canonical each page declares in <link rel=canonical>/og:url/schema.org url matched no rule and 404'd. Live GSC 2026-08-01, 16-month window: all 4 detail URLs in both forms are 'URL is unknown to Google, last crawled Never'; the /proyectos/ hub is 'Submitted and indexed' with 0 clicks / 7 impressions / pos 5.7. Semrush: 0 referring domains on deep URLs.
Expected_Impact: Closes 4 dead canonical URLs and one two-hop redirect chain. No index equity at risk; the hub keeps its 301.
Implementation_Guidance: Done. See the /proyectos/ block in v2/public/_redirects: all 4 slugs 301 in BOTH URL forms, three to /projects/ and buenaventura-ritz-reserve to /projects/buenaventura-resort-cocle (same-entity match); hub and index.html 301 to /projects/. 301 not 410 because Google has never crawled these, so there is nothing to de-index and the only remaining traffic is human. netlify.toml's /articles/proyectos/* rule now goes to /projects/ in one hop instead of chaining, and /co/* 301s to / on the same reasoning.
Risk: Low - every affected URL is either unknown to Google or keeps the destination it already had.
Validation_Method: Confirm /proyectos/sanctuary-residences and its .html form both 301 to /projects/, /proyectos/buenaventura-ritz-reserve 301s to /projects/buenaventura-resort-cocle, /articles/proyectos/* reaches /projects/ in ONE hop, and /co/* 301s to /. The old 'all 4 slugs return 200' check is void.

Issue: geo-route edge function advertises the locale pages being deleted
Evidence: netlify/edge-functions/geo-route.ts injects a dismissible 'Switch to your language' banner on / , /articles/* and /projects/* for visitors from ES/PT/DE-speaking countries, linking to /es/, /pt/ and /de/ URLs. Once T-02 ships those URLs return 410.
Expected_Impact: Prevents sending a large share of Panamanian, Colombian, Mexican, Spanish, Brazilian and German visitors to a 410 page.
Implementation_Guidance: Disable or remove the language-banner half of geo-route in the SAME deploy as the 410 rules. The per-jurisdiction cookie-banner logic in the same function is unrelated and should be retained — separate the two concerns rather than deleting the whole edge function. Note the function already exempts bots, so this is a pure UX fix with no crawler impact.
Risk: Medium if missed — Panama is the #2 country by clicks and maps to 'es' in the function's country table.
Validation_Method: Visit / with an es-ES Accept-Language and a PA geo; confirm no language banner renders

Issue: v2 has no article content — merging is safe, cutting over is not
Evidence: Supabase query on the v2 project returns 1 article (titled-vs-rights-of-possession), 15 areas, 31 projects (13 published). v1 has 85 English articles. Coverage check of the 30 v1 URLs that earn traffic (clicks>0 or impressions>=100) found 0 covered by a live v2 equivalent, 0 drafted, 30 with no v2 equivalent at all.
Expected_Impact: Distinguishes two things that are easy to conflate: merging the branch, and pointing the domain at it.
Implementation_Guidance: MERGING v2-redesign to main is safe today: netlify.toml sets publish = 'project' (the v1 static directory) and the branch does not modify netlify.toml or project/, so the live site is unaffected by the merge. CUTTING OVER is gated on List A of 12-v2-migration-plan.md — the 14 URLs holding page-1 positions on property-relevant queries. NOT all 30: the full set produces only ~11 clicks/month, so traffic alone does not justify blocking. Lists B (rewrite anyway) and C (expat utility, near-zero lead value) are non-blocking.
Risk: Critical if conflated. Cutting over before List A exists loses page-1 positions on the property queries; cutting over is NOT gated on the utility pages despite their higher impression count.
Validation_Method: Re-run v2/scripts/_coverage-check.mjs; require 0 gaps across List A before changing the publish target

Issue: Port script: project/data.js -> Supabase articles
Evidence: v1 article bodies are already structured data in PANAMA_DATA.articleBodies (84/84 articles have one), not HTML requiring extraction. Closed block taxonomy: plain string (paragraph), {h}, {quote}, {table}, {chart,caption,alt}. PANAMA_DATA.articles carries id, category, title, excerpt, metaDescription, author, date, read, cover, faqs, lang. The faqs shape {q,a} already matches the v2 articles.faqs jsonb column.
Expected_Impact: Turns a ~30-article writing project into roughly a day of scripted work, which is what makes migrating the low-traffic pages worth doing at all.
Implementation_Guidance: Map the 5 body block types to the v2 body column; map 19 v1 categories to the 4 v2 categories (buying/residency/money/living) per the table in 12-v2-migration-plan.md. Two rules: 'Real Estate by Location' articles fold into /areas/{slug} rather than becoming articles, since v2 already has 15 area records and location intent belongs on area hubs; the nationality-slice articles (panama-para-*, comprar-imovel-*, etc.) are NOT ported because they are marked Consolidate. Carry faqs across unchanged.
Risk: Low. Idempotent by slug; run against a Supabase branch first.
Validation_Method: Row counts per category match expectation; spot-check 5 ported articles for block fidelity; re-run coverage check

Issue: Repo project/ is not byte-identical to production
Evidence: The live page /articles/boquete-panama-real-estate.html serves a full hreflang cluster and 4 JSON-LD blocks. The repo copy at project/articles/boquete-panama-real-estate.html (6,739 bytes) contains the BEGIN_ARTICLE_META block but no hreflang, and git diff main...v2-redesign shows no difference in project/. netlify.toml declares no build command.
Expected_Impact: Unmanaged drift between the repository and production means an edit to project/ may not produce the expected live result, and a redeploy could silently revert injected SEO markup.
Implementation_Guidance: Establish where the injected markup comes from before editing project/ files: check for a build command configured in the Netlify UI (which overrides the absence of one in netlify.toml), or confirm whether scripts/inject-*.mjs are run manually and the output committed on a different branch. Then commit the generated output or declare the build in netlify.toml so the pipeline is reproducible. Until this is resolved, prefer netlify.toml redirect rules over project/ file edits — config applies at the edge regardless of which content is published.
Risk: Medium — a redeploy from a clean checkout could drop hreflang and JSON-LD from every article.
Validation_Method: Diff a fetched production page against its repo counterpart for 3 sample URLs; reconcile before any content deploy

Issue: v2 generateMetadata emits only title and description
Evidence: v2/app/[category]/[slug]/page.tsx generateMetadata returns { title, description } only — no canonical, no openGraph, no alternates.
Expected_Impact: Missing canonicals on a database-driven site invites duplicate-URL indexing (query params, pagination).
Implementation_Guidance: Extend generateMetadata to set alternates.canonical, openGraph (title/description/url/type/images) and twitter. metadataBase is already set correctly in layout.tsx.
Risk: Low
Validation_Method: View source on deployed pages; Search Console URL Inspection 'User-declared canonical'

Issue: No GA4 property exists for this domain
Evidence: Google Analytics account summaries list digitalsecretary.io, jobsnag.*, Casa de Empleo, chefgoya, LeyConsulta, Sr22, PescaYa, mdcalculator, flyfishing507 — there is no panamarealestateguide.com property.
Expected_Impact: Without this there is no conversion measurement at all; lead attribution is impossible.
Implementation_Guidance: Create a GA4 property. Define conversion events: consultation_submit, project_inquiry, checklist_download, newsletter_signup, whatsapp_click. Mark each as a key event. Link to Search Console. Add a lead-quality dimension captured from the form (budget band, timeline, area).
Risk: Low
Validation_Method: GA4 DebugView; confirm each key event fires once per genuine submission

Issue: Panama vs Panama City, Florida SERP ambiguity
Evidence: Semrush SERP analysis for 'panama real estate' returns zillow.com/panama-city-fl/ at position 7 — Google is mixing the country with the Florida city.
Expected_Impact: Correct entity disambiguation improves relevance for the highest-value head terms.
Implementation_Guidance: Consistently use disambiguating phrasing in titles, H1s and body ('Panama', 'Republic of Panama', 'Central America'). Add Organization schema with a Panama address. Note that 'real estate in panama central america' (590 vol, KD 15) and 'homes for sale in the republic of panama' (320 vol, KD 0) exist precisely because searchers are disambiguating — target them explicitly.
Risk: Low
Validation_Method: Position tracking on the disambiguated variants; monitor whether Florida results persist in the top 10

Issue: Core Web Vitals unmeasured on the v2 stack
Evidence: v1 is static HTML on Netlify with edge caching and etags — likely fine. v2 is an unreleased Next.js build; no field data exists because it is not deployed.
Expected_Impact: Prevents shipping a regression against a currently-fast static site.
Implementation_Guidance: Do not prescribe optimisations blind. Before launch, run Lighthouse and a bundle analysis on the v2 build. Specifically check: the hero-price-collage.png (currently an uncompressed PNG in v2/public) should be AVIF/WebP via next/image with explicit dimensions; confirm fonts are self-hosted with font-display:swap rather than the render-blocking fonts.googleapis.com <link> pattern used in v1.
Risk: Medium — v1 is genuinely fast; a heavy React rebuild can regress LCP.
Validation_Method: PageSpeed Insights lab + Search Console Core Web Vitals field data 28 days post-launch; compare against v1 baseline captured before cutover

Issue: Internal link depth and orphan risk after pruning
Evidence: Consolidating 57 URLs and deleting 405 will strip a large share of existing internal links. Any surviving link that points at a 410'd URL is now a dead link, not just an unindexed one.
Expected_Impact: Prevents newly orphaned pages and preserves crawl paths.
Implementation_Guidance: After the pruning pass, recrawl and assert every Keep/Improve URL is reachable within 3 clicks of the homepage. Build the internal-linking blueprint (pillar -> cluster -> area -> project, and back) before removing links, not after.
Risk: Medium
Validation_Method: Screaming Frog crawl depth report; assert zero orphans among Keep/Improve URLs

Issue: hreflang will break when translations are noindexed
Evidence: v1 emits a 5-way hreflang cluster (en/es/pt/de/x-default) on every article. Noindexing the alternates while leaving hreflang in place sends contradictory signals.
Expected_Impact: Removes a conflicting-directive problem.
Implementation_Guidance: Remove hreflang annotations at the same time as the noindex rollout, in one deploy. If a Spanish site is revived later, do it as a deliberate, human-written subset — not a full mirror.
Risk: Medium — must ship together with T-02, not separately.
Validation_Method: Search Console International Targeting report; validate no hreflang errors remain

Issue: No log-file analysis available
Evidence: Netlify hosting; no access to raw request logs was available in this session.
Expected_Impact: Would confirm crawl-budget waste on the 405 translated URLs empirically.
Implementation_Guidance: Enable Netlify Log Drains to a store you can query, or use Search Console Crawl Stats as a proxy. Re-check crawl distribution 30 days after T-02 ships.
Risk: Low
Validation_Method: Search Console Settings > Crawl stats: crawl requests by response and by file type before/after
